pages.text: Bronze Age Akrotiri Is Greek's Pompeii Skip to main content History | November 3, 2026 Greece Has Its Own Pompeii, and the Ruins Tell a Captivating Story of a Sophisticated, Seafaring Bronze Age Society The Thera volcano, on modern-day Santorini, buried Akrotiri in ash in the 17th or 16th century B.C.E. The eruption was one of the largest in recorded history The ruins of Akrotiri, a Bronze Age settlement on what is now the Greek island of Santorini Westend61 via Getty Images The ruins of Akrotiri, a Bronze Age settlement on what is now the Greek island of Santorini Westend61 via Getty Images The earth rumbled for days. Inhabitants of the seafaring Bronze Age settlement of Akrotiri watched smoke plume from Thera , a long-dormant volcano on what is now the Greek island of Santorini . People gathered their belongings and safely stored the valuables they were forced to leave behind. Then they fled by boat to nearby islands. When these minor earthquakes and eruptions subsided, residents returned to Akrotiri, collecting materials for reconstruction and beginning the arduous process of repairing the damage . But the ground continued to tremble. As conditions worsened , they made the difficult decision to flee once more, hopeful that their homes would survive the coming devastation. When Thera erupted again, the explosion was so powerful that it destroyed Akrotiri, burying the settlement (and the island that shared the volcano’s name) in some 200 feet of ash and pumice stone. pages.text: Bryce Miller returning to Mariners' rotation Skip to Content PHILADELPHIA -- Bryce Miller had some reflective perspective when discussing his much-anticipated return from the injured list, slated for Tuesday night against the Phillies at Citizens Bank Park. On the one hand, it has been a brutal year filled with pain in the right-hander’s pitching elbow, a setback that necessitated a second IL stint and a lack of production that at times made him a liability in the Mariners’ rotation. Yet on the other, if Miller can regain some semblance of his 2024 form down the stretch and help Seattle reach the postseason, he’ll look back on this year through a drastically different lens. “I can't change what's already been done,” Miller said, “and my only goal moving forward is not to get my ERA down to three-something or any of that. It's just go out, compete, finish strong and get us into the postseason and see how far we can go. And whatever the numbers are at the end, for me, it is what it is. “We'll restart next year. But I just want to go out and finish strong and go out and pitch like I know I can.” Based on the schedule’s mathematics – and with the Mariners intending for Miller to operate on a six-day routine for now – he could make roughly six more starts in the regular season. If Seattle does play into October, his role could shift to the bullpen in a shortened series. pages.text: Bryce Miller shut down with left oblique injury Skip to Content PEORIA, Ariz. -- The good news for Bryce Miller is that his arm has felt great throughout Spring Training . The not-so-good news is that he recently suffered left side oblique inflammation that will preclude him from making his next Cactus League start. Miller received a platelet rich plasma shot on Friday night after undergoing imaging that revealed the issue, which he experienced during the first inning of his Cactus start on Thursday. He’ll be sidelined from throwing through the weekend then could begin playing light catch after. But it’s unclear when he’ll be back on the mound in Cactus play. “It's something he usually goes through when he first starts to ramp up for camp,” said Mariners general manager Justin Hollander, who said that the club will re-evaluate Miller’s status in seven days. Chaimbeul grew up on the Isle of Skye, Scotland, speaking Gaelic and learning the Highland pipes before falling in love with the bellows-blown bagpipe she plays today. Drones are forever with this instrument, but Chaimbeul amplifies, manipulates and darkens the harmonics and frequencies of these pipe drones with effects pedals and contact mics that capture her percussive tapping on the chanter. Buildings The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) focuses on buildings primarily through the lens of energy efficiency, sustainability, and safety. The Building Technologies Office (BTO) leads efforts to enhance energy efficiency in both residential and commercial structures by developing and deploying advanced building technologies, promoting energy codes and standards, and supporting programs for energy upgrades. How Do Buildings Use Energy? Buildings use energy for heating and cooling indoor spaces, powering lighting, running appliances and equipment, and supporting daily operations. Larger facilities may also use energy for ventilation, refrigeration, computing systems, and other building services. These energy needs make buildings a key part of overall energy demand. Why Buildings Matter Buildings affect how energy is used across communities, businesses, and public services. Improvements in building design, equipment, and operations can help reduce waste, improve performance, and support more effective energy use over time. pages.text: Bunion facts: Causes, symptoms, and treatment | National Geographic Premium HEALTH Why do we have bunions? Blame an evolutionary toe failure. For millennia, people have suffered from bunions, a painful condition that’s uniquely human. Here’s why—and how to ease the pain. A colored x-ray image highlights bunions in the feet of a 54-year-old patient. The foot deformity may affect up to a quarter of the modern adult population. ZEPHYR/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY By Erin Blakemore Last updated October 14, 2025 Bunions have plagued human feet since ancient times. A brief glimpse at archaeology and history points to their presence, from prehistoric footprints in England to ancient Egyptian mummies with bony bumps . A whopping 27 percent of burials in and around Cambridge, England, during the 14th and 15th centuries showed skeletal evidence of bunions, compared with just 6 percent in earlier centuries. The likely culprit? Researchers attribute the difference to the medieval emergence of “poulaine” shoes , long leather footwear with a pointed tip. But why do we get them in the first place—and why haven’t we figured out how they’re caused or cured without surgery? Here’s how our feet developed one of their most common woes—and why they still perplex scientists. What are bunions? Also known as hallux valgus , bunions are a type of foot problem in which one of the toes—usually the hallux, or big toe—leans in toward the other toes, widening the foot as the big toe joint begins protruding from its side. These are the first public-use statistics that use W-2 filings to combine longitudinal business data with population-level worker demographic data to classify firms based on the characteristics of their workers. The BDS-HC tables describe the relationship between business dynamics and workforce composition for nearly all non-farm employer businesses in the United States from 2000 to 2023. Each table reports all economic outcomes covered by the BDS, including establishment openings and closings, firm startups and shutdowns, and job creation and destruction, for different groups of firms based on their workforce composition. Separate tables are available based on the share of a firm’s workforce that belongs to each category within six demographic characteristics: age, sex, race, ethnicity, nativity, and education. Tables also provide statistics broken out by the interaction between workforce composition and business characteristics, such as the establishment’s industrial sector and state and the firm’s size and age. pages.text: Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) Skip Navigation Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) September 2026 The Business Dynamics Statistics of Single Unit Firms with Revenue (BDS-SU-REV) is an experimental data product extending the set of statistics published by the Business Dynamics Statistics (BDS) program. The BDS-SU-REV provides year-over-year changes in employment, payroll, and revenue for each quarter of the year for businesses that operate in one location (single-units) and file their taxes under a single Employer Identification Number (EIN). This product relies on IRS annual tax filings to collect revenue information and IRS quarterly tax filings to collect employment and payroll information for the pay periods including March 12 th , June 12 th , September 12 th , and December 12 th . Year-over-year employment and payroll changes are calculated between the same point in year t and year t-1 (i.e., June 12 th year t-1 to June 12 th year t, etc.). Employment and payroll growth is labeled as job and pay creation respectively and employment and payroll decline as job and pay destruction. A novel innovation in the BDS-SU-REV is the incorporation of annual revenue data for single-establishment firms that consistently maintain positive employment levels each quarter. A positive annual growth in revenue is categorized as revenue creation, while negative growth is categorized as revenue destruction. Jump to: Data Definitions

Beginning with the 2016 survey year, however, the accommodation and food service data are now collected and published through the Service Annual Survey (SAS) . Frequency The supplement is conducted every five years. Specifically, it occurs in years ending in "2" and "7," just like the Economic Census . Coverage The estimates include data only for retail businesses with paid employees (that are located in the United States). The BTOS sample consists of approximately 1.2 million businesses split into six panels (approximately 200,000 cases per panel). The BTOS is comprised of a set of core questions and supplemental content, which is added as needed. The BTOS collects information on a broad range of business conditions. Data collected from September 11, 2023 to present include all employer businesses (single location and multi-location) in the U.S. economy, excluding farms. pages.description: Peter Bradshaw: Reasonably amusing, with 2-D acting and writing, and Day-Glo pink and blue colour schemes.
pages.text: But I'm a Cheerleader | Movies | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Movies This article is more than 25 years old Review But I'm a Cheerleader This article is more than 25 years old Peter Bradshaw Thu 12 Apr 2001 21.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google D irector and co-writer Jamie Babbit makes her feature debut with this satire of America's creepy Christian "sexual reorientation" camps, where confused teens are sent so that their nascent gayness can be deprogrammed out of them. Natasha Lyonne plays Megan, a cheerleader who hugs her fellow pom-pom-botherers inappropriately and hates making out with her jock boyfriend. He and Megan's family arrange an "intervention" where she is confronted with her shameful tendencies and sent to the True Directions camp, run by two smug tyrants in Straight Is Great T-shirts, played by Cathy Moriarty and RuPaul (here out of drag), clearly repressed gays themselves. Once there, Megan falls for a girl with the interesting name of Graham, played by Clea DuVall. As in all therapy boot-camp movies - such as Girl, Interrupted, in which DuVall had a role - there has to be a wild child with whom the heroine makes a connection. This is Graham's role. It's reasonably amusing, with 2-D acting and writing, and Day-Glo pink and blue colour schemes. But it could have been funnier, and I would have preferred to know more in documentary terms about the actual reality of these terrible camps, rather than sit through this heavy-handed and oddly lenient comedy. Then read on. Which train ticket is the best choice for me? As a general rule, the earlier you can buy a ticket, the better the price you can get. If you know the date and time you wish to travel, then an Advance ticket will be suitable. For more flexibility, Off-Peak and Super Off-Peak tickets and Anytime tickets will be a better option, as you are not limited to a specific date or train. For more information about getting the most affordable ticket for your journey, see below. Advance tickets These must be bought in advance and are only valid on the date and train specified. They are sold in limited numbers, subject to availability and on a first come, first served basis. You can usually buy an Advance ticket up to 12 weeks ahead of travel, and they are still available until the day of travel on many routes – sometimes up to 10 minutes before departure. They offer a great deal if you know exactly when you want to travel. Find out more about Advance tickets . Off-Peak and Super Off-Peak tickets These good value tickets can be bought at any time and allow you to travel on any permitted train during off-peak hours. If an Off-Peak or Super Off-Peak ticket is available for your journey, journey planners will make them available to purchase. In general, Off-Peak hours begin at 09:30 from Monday to Friday in cities and large towns, and at 09:00 everywhere else.

pages.description: Whether it’s a short hop across the Channel or an overland expedition to the furthest reaches of Europe, some of the richest travel experiences happen when you skip the flight.
pages.text: By Land and Sea—17 European Trips From London | National Geographic By Oliver Smith Published October 24, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Today, it’s easier to travel further and faster around Europe than ever before — to board a flight and effectively parachute yourself into a new destination. But by travelling overland, be it by ferry, train or car, on a bike or on foot, you’re able to observe the slow, subtle changes at ground level with every accumulated mile. Overland travel by rail is also easier than it’s ever been, thanks to an ever-expanding network of high-speed and sleeper trains across Europe. You might board a morning Eurostar at London St Pancras International and that same day be joining a midnight crawl of Madrid’s tapas bars or standing beneath Milan’s hulking Duomo as stars twinkle above its white marble facade. Ferries, too, offer perspectives unfamiliar to those at the cruising altitude of an airliner, whether that’s witnessing the green coast of northern Spain unravelling out of the blue horizons of Biscay or seeing Icelandic volcanoes peek over grey North Atlantic waves.
